assertions.statement: When the request authorizes an edit and the condition supports that responsibility, the target file is changed rather than only described.
A format-only request preserves wording, order, link destinations, code, commands, identifiers, and meaning.
Does not introduce prose hard wrapping based on an implicit line-length limit.
Normalizes the requested blank-line, list, fence, table, and final-newline inconsistencies that are safe under the supplied profile.
Adds half-width spaces at the requested Japanese/alphabetic or Japanese/numeric boundaries without changing protected token internals.
Preserves frontmatter, URLs, link destinations, inline code, fenced code, commands, and identifier contents.
Does not silently choose a heading relationship, section meaning, punctuation policy, or other unstated semantic decision.
Makes a material unresolved structural decision or unsupported static responsibility visible instead of reporting complete success.
Performs an explicitly authorized wording change when the supplied fact is sufficient, and does not reject it merely because formatting is also requested.
A review-only request reports structural readability observations without modifying the fixture.
Does not present CommonMark as the source of universal recommended, context-dependent, or discouraged writing styles.

verdict_policy.critical_failure: Any failed critical assertion fails the applicable condition for that case.
verdict_policy.partial: A condition is partial when it satisfies all critical assertions but misses at least one applicable non-critical assertion.
verdict_policy.not_applicable: A responsibility outside a static tool's declared scope is recorded as not_applicable and is not counted as pass.
verdict_policy.render_equivalence: For format-only fixtures, compare rendered structure before and after with the recorded parser. A changed render hash overrides a prose grader's content-preservation pass.
verdict_policy.comparison: Do not collapse the matrix into one score. Compare deterministic coverage, judgment coverage, critical regressions, and routing separately.
